brief.headline: Close a ₹28.69 L gap to our best plastic-packaging prices — then swap 15-day faster payment for a 4.5% discount

priceAsk.summary: Benchmark Cincorp's prices down to what we already pay Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic on the same rigid-plastic items
priceAsk.target: ₹28.69 L annual saving by matching best prices we pay
priceAsk.basis: We pay Mars Plastics ₹0.81/NOS for the PP cap (Cincorp charges ₹1.08, a 33.2% gap), ₹1.38/NOS for the HDPE bottle (Cincorp ₹1.53, 10.7% gap), and Premier Plastic ₹0.35/NOS for the measuring cup (Cincorp ₹0.46, 30.6% gap). These are our proven market prices for identical rigid-plastic SKUs — Cincorp should match them.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 Days After Receipt to 30 days in exchange for a ~4.5% discount, or to 60 days to free working capital for us
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Shifting to 30 days frees ₹16.02 L of our working capital; extending to 60 days would cost us ₹16.02 L but gives us a negotiating chip if they need longer runway

brief.financialLeverage: Cincorp is a small, levered manufacturer (₹4.11 Cr revenue, D/E 1.13x) in the grey Altman-Z distress zone (1.83) with 6.0% net margin — half the 15.0% peer median — and negative free cash flow of ₹-79.14 L. We are 47.43% of their revenue, so we are a critical customer they cannot afford to lose. Their borrowing cost is 4.54%, meaning early payment is worth that much to them. However, their thin margin and distress signal mean a hard price squeeze risks tipping them into real trouble. Lead with payment-for-discount swaps and volume commitment, not brute force — but the volume share gives us real leverage to close the ₹28.69 L price gap and improve terms without breaking them.

evidence.point: We overpay by ₹28.69 L per year versus the best prices we already secure from other rigid-plastic suppliers
Our largest price gap is 33.2% on the PP cap — we pay Cincorp ₹1.08/NOS while Mars Plastics charges ₹0.81/NOS
Cincorp earns a 6.0% net margin, well below the 15.0% peer median, so their pricing power is already weak
We represent 47.43% of Cincorp's ₹4.11 Cr revenue — we are their biggest customer by far
Cincorp's Altman-Z score of 1.83 places them in the grey distress zone, signaling financial fragility
They carry debt at D/E 1.13x and a 4.54% effective borrowing cost, so faster payment is worth roughly that rate to them

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100), already a second-source candidate for pharma bottles and caps — a direct, robust replacement

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed, profitable rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) specializing in pharma containers — strong continuity and scale

alternates.name: Mars Plastics
alternates.why: Already our best-price supplier for the PP cap (₹0.81/NOS) and HDPE bottle (₹1.38/NOS) — proven capability on the exact SKUs where Cincorp overcharges

risks: Cincorp is small (₹4.11 Cr revenue) and in the grey distress zone (Altman-Z 1.83) — pushing too hard on price could trigger a supplier failure and disrupt our supply of rigid-plastic packaging
We are 47.43% of their revenue, so if we walk or cut volume sharply, they may not survive — verify we have Manjushree or Mold-Tek ready to absorb volume before threatening a switch
Negative free cash flow of ₹-79.14 L and D/E 1.13x mean they are liquidity-constrained — any extension of payment terms beyond 45 days could worsen their cash crisis

Their 6.0% margin is half the peer median, so a ₹28.69 L annual price cut (roughly 14.7% of our ₹1.95 Cr spend) may exceed what they can absorb without going into loss — structure the ask as a phased glide-path or tie it to faster payment to ease the hit
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more per year than our best rigid-plastic prices — let's work together to close that gap and find a payment structure that works for both of us.
